phrases.translation: Alif-Lãm-Mĩm
phrases.explanation: These opening letters belong to the form of the revealed text. Their precise meaning is not settled with certainty here, so readers should avoid presenting a private theory as established fact. Their presence invites attention to the revelation while leaving their precise significance to Allah, whose knowledge exceeds ours.

phrases.translation: Allah! There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him
phrases.explanation: This declaration reserves divinity and worship for Allah alone. Everything else is created, owned, and dependent, so no idol, person, angel, or heavenly body can share His lordship. The verse establishes His uniqueness before the chapter answers claims that confuse a created servant with the Creator.

phrases.translation: —the Ever-Living, All-Sustaining
phrases.explanation: Allah’s life never ends or suffers interruption, unlike every created living being. He also sustains, guards, and manages every affair by His power. These descriptions give believers a firm basis for worship and trust, since the One they serve remains alive and actively upholds all that exists.

phrases.translation: He has revealed to you ˹O Prophet˺ the Book in truth
phrases.explanation: The Book referred to here is the Qur’an, revealed to Muhammad with truth rather than conjecture. Its message addresses disputed matters honestly and provides reliable guidance. Revelation is Allah’s action, while the Prophet receives and conveys what his Lord has sent to him. Its mystery therefore teaches intellectual humility.

phrases.translation: confirming what came before it
phrases.explanation: The Qur’an confirms the revelations that came before it because the same Lord sent guidance through His messengers. Divine revelation is fundamentally consistent in its witness to Allah and His truth. This confirmation does not make the Qur’an dependent on human religious authorities for its authority.

phrases.translation: as He revealed the Torah and the Gospel
phrases.explanation: The Torah was given to Moses and the Gospel to Jesus before the Qur’an. Mentioning them places the Prophet’s message within a continuing history of divine guidance. Earlier scripture served to direct people, affirm Allah’s oneness, and explain the duties His messengers taught. It remains revelation from beginning to end.

phrases.translation: previously, as a guide for people, and ˹also˺ revealed the Standard ˹to distinguish between right and wrong˺.
phrases.explanation: Earlier revelation guided people, and the Standard distinguishes truth from falsehood where communities disagree. This separating function comes through decisive divine clarification and guidance. Guidance therefore involves more than possessing a text. It enables sincere readers to recognize truth and reject claims that contradict Allah’s revelation.

phrases.translation: Surely those who reject Allah’s revelations will suffer a severe torment.
phrases.explanation: Rejecting Allah’s revelations and the proofs they contain carries a severe consequence. In this passage, the warning especially concerns denying divine evidence and making claims about Jesus that contradict his servanthood. The punishment is linked to persistent rejection after truth has been made clear. The warning therefore calls for repentance.

phrases.translation: For Allah is Almighty, capable of punishment
phrases.explanation: Allah’s might means that no person can escape His judgment or find protection against His decree. His ability to punish is not limited by wealth, status, or supporters. This closing description gives weight to the warning while affirming that His power remains governed by perfect justice.

phrases.translation: Surely nothing on earth or in the heavens is hidden from Allah
phrases.explanation: Allah knows everything throughout the earth and heavens, including what people conceal in their speech and intentions. No false claim about Him or His messengers is hidden from Him. This complete knowledge leaves no basis for imagining that public argument or private pretense can obscure the truth from God.

phrases.translation: He is the One Who shapes you in the wombs of your mothers as He wills.
phrases.explanation: Allah forms every human being in the womb according to His will. Development before birth displays creative power that no parent or human being controls independently. In the chapter’s context, this also directs attention to Allah’s ability to create as He chooses without making any created child His equal.

phrases.translation: There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him
phrases.explanation: The One who forms creation alone deserves worship. A created person cannot possess independent divinity or share Allah’s sovereignty. This statement therefore rejects both idolatry and any attempt to turn Jesus or another servant of Allah into a second divine being beside the Creator. This truth applies to every created being.

phrases.translation: —the Almighty, All-Wise
phrases.explanation: Allah is Almighty, so no creature can frustrate His authority or provide refuge from Him. He is also All-Wise in His actions, guidance, and establishment of proof. Power and wisdom belong together here, assuring readers that His rule is neither weak nor arbitrary. Nothing in His rule lacks purpose.

phrases.translation: He is the One Who has revealed to you ˹O Prophet˺ the Book, of which some verses are precise
phrases.explanation: Allah revealed the Qur’an to the Prophet with verses whose meanings include clear, decisive teachings. These precise passages communicate guidance directly and provide a secure basis for belief and conduct. Readers should begin with what revelation makes clear rather than building their religion on speculation.

phrases.translation: —they are the foundation of the Book
phrases.explanation: The precise verses are described as the Book’s foundation because its central guidance rests upon them. They anchor understanding and help readers approach the rest of revelation responsibly. Difficult passages should not be used to overturn established truths about Allah, His messengers, or accountable human conduct.

phrases.translation: —while others are elusive.
phrases.explanation: Other verses are elusive in that their complete significance is not equally accessible to every reader. This does not make them false or meaningless. Their presence calls for humility, careful interpretation, and willingness to leave matters of unseen knowledge to Allah instead of forcing a confident answer.

phrases.translation: Those with deviant hearts follow the elusive verses seeking ˹to spread˺ doubt through their ˹false˺ interpretations
phrases.explanation: People whose hearts turn away from sound guidance may exploit elusive passages to create confusion and support interpretations driven by their desires. Their aim is doubt and dispute rather than sincere understanding. The warning concerns dishonest use of scripture, not humble questions or careful scholarly inquiry.

phrases.translation: —but none grasps their ˹full˺ meaning except Allah.
phrases.explanation: Allah possesses complete knowledge of what remains hidden from human readers. This limitation restrains speculative claims about unseen realities and disputed details. A person should not present conjecture as certain revelation, especially when the purpose is to win an argument or unsettle the faith of others.

phrases.translation: As for those well-grounded in knowledge, they say, “We believe in this ˹Quran˺
phrases.explanation: Those firmly grounded in knowledge respond to the Qur’an with faith rather than arrogance. Their learning does not make them imagine that they know everything. They accept the revelation, recognize its divine source, and remain steady where their own understanding reaches a limit. This is the mark of mature faith.

phrases.translation: —it is all from our Lord.”
phrases.explanation: Clear and elusive verses alike come from the same Lord. Believers therefore do not treat one part as divine and dismiss another because it puzzles them. This confession joins intellectual humility with trust, allowing the whole Book to remain guidance even when human comprehension is incomplete.

phrases.translation: But none will be mindful ˹of this˺ except people of reason
phrases.explanation: People of reason are those who take heed and allow revelation to restrain their speech and assumptions. Understanding is shown through humility before divine knowledge, not through reckless claims. The verse closes by making reflection and admonition essential to a responsible reading of difficult passages.

phrases.translation: ˹They say,˺ “Our Lord! Do not let our hearts deviate after you have guided us.
phrases.explanation: The well-grounded believers ask Allah to keep their hearts from turning away after receiving guidance. Their prayer acknowledges that faith needs divine protection and continued steadfastness. Having knowledge does not remove humility or the need to seek help against confusion, desire, and spiritual deviation. Their dependence on Him continues every day.

phrases.translation: Grant us Your mercy.
phrases.explanation: The requested mercy includes Allah’s help to remain firm upon the truth. Believers need more than correct information. They need grace that strengthens faith, preserves sound judgment, and supports obedience. The request follows naturally from their concern about hearts deviating after guidance. Such mercy sustains the whole of faith.

phrases.translation: You are indeed the Giver ˹of all bounties˺
phrases.explanation: Allah is the generous Giver whose gifts include guidance, mercy, and steadfastness. This title gives the supplicants confidence without making them presumptuous. They ask because He bestows freely, not because their knowledge or devotion places Him under any obligation to them. Their hope rests upon divine generosity alone.

phrases.translation: Our Lord! You will certainly gather all humanity for the ˹promised˺ Day
phrases.explanation: The believers affirm that Allah will gather all humanity for the promised Day. Resurrection and judgment are therefore central to their understanding of revelation. Faith in the Book includes accepting accountability before God rather than treating this life as the whole of human existence. Every person will be included after death.

phrases.translation: —about which there is no doubt.
phrases.explanation: The promised Day is not uncertain speculation. Its coming is sure because Allah has declared it. This certainty strengthens the believers’ prayers and gives moral seriousness to their response to clear and elusive verses alike. It therefore calls for preparation rather than doubt or delay.

phrases.translation: Surely Allah does not break His promise.”
phrases.explanation: Allah does not fail to fulfil what He promises. His truthfulness assures believers of the gathering they have just confessed and of every other reliable divine promise. Hope and warning in revelation both rest on His unfailing word. His promise rests upon perfect knowledge and power.

phrases.translation: Indeed, neither the wealth nor children of the disbelievers will be of any benefit to them against Allah
phrases.explanation: Wealth and children cannot protect persistent rejecters from Allah’s judgment or purchase an escape from punishment. The verse addresses people who deny recognized truth, not a claim that family and property are evil. It exposes the false security placed in worldly attachments when they are treated as ultimate protection.

phrases.translation: —and they will be the fuel for the Fire
phrases.explanation: Those who persist in rejection face the Fire, where their own selves and deeds bring them to its fuel rather than rescue. The image reverses worldly expectations of power and inheritance. Neither possessions nor descendants can change the outcome of unrepented denial before Allah. No worldly advantage can reverse that judgment.

phrases.translation: Their fate will be like that of the people of Pharaoh and those before them
phrases.explanation: The fate awaiting persistent rejecters resembles that of Pharaoh’s people and earlier nations who followed the same pattern of denial. The comparison warns that their worldly advantages cannot alter the outcome. Earlier examples make the consequence visible through history rather than leaving it as an abstract threat.

phrases.translation: —they all rejected Our signs, so Allah seized them for their sins.
phrases.explanation: Those earlier communities rejected Allah’s signs and were seized because of their sins. Their punishment followed accountable conduct, not arbitrary divine action. The verse connects denial with its moral consequences and reminds later readers that possessing scripture, wealth, or social strength provides no immunity. History therefore becomes a warning for attentive readers.

phrases.translation: And Allah is severe in punishment
phrases.explanation: Allah’s punishment is severe because His authority is complete and His judgment cannot be resisted. This closing warning reinforces the seriousness of rejecting His signs. It also assures oppressed believers that apparent power does not place wrongdoers beyond divine reach. His verdict is always founded upon truth.

phrases.translation: ˹O Prophet!˺ Tell the disbelievers, “Soon you will be overpowered and driven to Hell
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is instructed to warn persistent disbelievers that they will ultimately be overcome and gathered toward Hell. Their present confidence is therefore not final. The announcement comes through revelation, making it a call to reconsider before judgment rather than a prediction based on human military strength.

phrases.translation: —what an evil place to rest!”
phrases.explanation: Hell is described as an evil resting place, reversing the idea of arrival at safety or comfort. The destination offers none of the security people ordinarily seek in a home. This brief conclusion intensifies the warning and leaves the responsibility for heeding it with those addressed.

phrases.translation: Indeed, there was a sign for you in the two armies that met in battle
phrases.explanation: The meeting of two armies at Badr provided a visible sign of Allah’s support. A smaller believing force faced a stronger opponent, yet the outcome could not be explained simply by numbers. The event invites readers to recognize divine aid within a real historical struggle.

phrases.translation: —one fighting for the cause of Allah and the other in denial.
phrases.explanation: One army fought in Allah’s cause while the other persisted in denial. The verse distinguishes the two sides by faith and purpose, not merely by tribe or military identity. Their opposing commitments give the encounter its moral significance as a sign for later audiences. Badr therefore carried meaning beyond the battlefield itself.

phrases.translation: The believers saw their enemy twice their number.
phrases.explanation: The believers saw the opposing force as twice their own number, emphasizing how daunting the confrontation appeared. Changing perceptions of the enemy’s number during the event are also discussed. Either way, the central lesson remains that visible superiority does not determine the outcome. Human estimates cannot limit divine assistance.

phrases.translation: But Allah supports with His victory whoever He wills.
phrases.explanation: Victory ultimately comes through Allah’s strengthening of whomever He wills. Human effort and preparation have their place, but they do not independently guarantee success. This truth prevents both pride in victory and despair when believers face apparently stronger opposition. The believing army experienced that truth directly at Badr.

phrases.translation: Surely in this is a lesson for people of insight
phrases.explanation: People of insight look beyond the surface of Badr and learn about reliance upon Allah. The event becomes instruction for anyone willing to reflect, not just a report about one battle. Spiritual perception recognizes divine support where a purely numerical reading would miss it. Such reflection strengthens trust without promoting passivity.

phrases.translation: The enjoyment of ˹worldly˺ desires
phrases.explanation: Human beings naturally feel attraction toward many enjoyable things in worldly life. The verse begins with desire itself, acknowledging how powerfully it can shape attention and choices. It does not immediately call every desired object evil, but prepares readers to judge worldly attraction by its final destination.

phrases.translation: —women, children, treasures of gold and silver, fine horses, cattle, and fertile land
phrases.explanation: Relationships, children, accumulated wealth, beautiful horses, livestock, and cultivated land represent familiar forms of affection, status, security, and abundance. The list speaks through things people readily value. Their diversity shows how easily the heart can become absorbed by this life in many different ways. Each can capture affection and distract from lasting priorities.

phrases.translation: —has been made appealing to people.
phrases.explanation: These attractions have been made appealing, so their pull is a real part of human experience. The danger arises when love for them leads someone to prefer worldly position over recognized truth. Enjoyment must therefore remain under the guidance of faith rather than becoming life’s governing purpose.

phrases.translation: These are the pleasures of this worldly life, but with Allah is the finest destination
phrases.explanation: Worldly pleasures are temporary, while the finest final destination is with Allah. The comparison does not deny present beauty, but places it on a limited scale. Lasting good should receive greater devotion than possessions and enjoyments that end with this life. The wise person therefore measures enjoyment by endurance and divine approval.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Shall I inform you of what is better than ˹all of˺ this?
phrases.explanation: The Prophet offers to tell people about something better than the worldly attractions just listed. This question redirects desire rather than simply condemning it. Believers are invited to compare temporary enjoyment with a reward that answers their deepest longing for lasting goodness. The answer expands their idea of what is truly desirable.

phrases.translation: Those mindful ˹of Allah˺ will have Gardens with their Lord under which rivers flow,
phrases.explanation: Those mindful of Allah are promised Gardens with flowing rivers in His presence and care. The image presents abundant life, beauty, and security. Unlike worldly gardens and wealth, this reward belongs to the Hereafter and is granted to people whose awareness of Allah shapes their conduct.

phrases.translation: to stay there forever, and pure spouses, along with Allah’s pleasure.”
phrases.explanation: The Gardens are everlasting and include pure companions and, above all, Allah’s pleasure. Permanence answers the loss attached to worldly enjoyment. Divine approval gives the reward its highest value, showing that Paradise is not merely luxury but a honoured relationship with the Lord. No temporary pleasure can equal that complete reward.

phrases.translation: And Allah is All-Seeing of ˹His˺ servants
phrases.explanation: Allah sees His servants, including the sincerity of their mindfulness, prayers, patience, and generosity. Nothing faithful is hidden from Him. This assurance connects the promised reward with divine knowledge of the people who strive for it, even when others do not notice their devotion. He also knows every struggle that sincerity requires.

phrases.translation: who pray, “Our Lord! We have believed
phrases.explanation: The servants described begin their prayer by affirming belief. Their request grows from faith rather than a claim of personal perfection. They approach Allah as believers who still recognize sin and need, joining confidence in Him with honest awareness of their shortcomings. Their words unite devotion with a continuing need for grace.

phrases.translation: so forgive our sins and protect us from the torment of the Fire.”
phrases.explanation: They ask for forgiveness and protection from the Fire because belief does not make them careless about accountability. The prayer seeks both pardon for what has passed and safety from its consequences. It models humble hope rather than either despair or presumption. Faith leads them to seek Allah rather than rely on themselves.

phrases.translation: ˹It is they˺ who are patient, sincere, obedient, and charitable
phrases.explanation: These believers remain patient through hardship, truthful in speech and faith, obedient in worship, and generous with what they possess. Their virtues cover inner steadiness, honesty, devotion, and social responsibility. The promised reward therefore responds to a complete pattern of faithful living rather than one isolated act.

phrases.translation: and who pray for forgiveness before dawn
phrases.explanation: Seeking forgiveness before dawn points to private worship at a quiet time when sincerity is especially visible. They end the night by acknowledging their faults and asking Allah to cover them. Regular repentance belongs alongside patience, truthfulness, obedience, and charity. Hidden devotion thus supports their visible righteousness.

phrases.translation: Allah ˹Himself˺ is a Witness that there is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him
phrases.explanation: Allah Himself bears witness that no being other than Him deserves divinity or worship. His testimony stands above every human claim, including claims of divine sonship or partnership. The verse grounds monotheism in His own declaration rather than in speculation about created beings. Everything besides Him remains created and dependent.

phrases.translation: —and so are the angels and people of knowledge.
phrases.explanation: Angels and people endowed with knowledge also witness to Allah’s oneness. Their testimony agrees with His truth and shows that genuine knowledge leads toward monotheism rather than confusion about Him. The reference to knowledgeable people emphasizes understanding grounded in revelation. Their witness is consistent with the truth revealed through the prophets.

phrases.translation: He is the Maintainer of justice.
phrases.explanation: Allah maintains justice among His creatures. His rule and judgment are therefore not expressions of arbitrary power. The statement reassures believers that accountability is equitable while warning wrongdoers that they cannot expect favouritism or corruption in His government. Nobody will be treated with partiality before Him.

phrases.translation: There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him
phrases.explanation: The repeated declaration reinforces that worship belongs to Allah alone. Repetition gives the truth emphasis after the mention of witnesses and justice. No created prophet, angel, or scholar changes this central confession, however honoured that servant may be. It leaves no room for divided worship or loyalty.

phrases.translation: —the Almighty, All-Wise
phrases.explanation: Allah’s might places Him beyond opposition, and His wisdom governs what He creates, commands, and judges. These names conclude the testimony by joining perfect authority with perfect purpose. His oneness is therefore tied to both His irresistible power and His wise guidance. Believers can therefore trust both His command and His judgment.

phrases.translation: Certainly, Allah’s only Way is Islam.
phrases.explanation: The way accepted by Allah is Islam, understood here as obedience and willing submission to Him. It is not merely a label inherited by a community. The verse calls people to devote worship and obedience sincerely to Allah in accordance with the guidance He sends.

phrases.translation: Those who were given the Scripture did not dispute ˹among themselves˺ out of mutual envy until knowledge came to them.
phrases.explanation: Some recipients of scripture disputed only after knowledge had reached them, driven by envy, rivalry, and desire for leadership. Their division is therefore not blamed on a lack of evidence. The passage criticizes knowing rejection and partisan ambition rather than sincere searching for truth. Knowledge makes the responsible choice especially serious.

phrases.translation: Whoever denies Allah’s signs, then surely Allah is swift in reckoning
phrases.explanation: Allah preserves every deed and can reckon with it without effort or delay. Those who deny His signs cannot escape accountability through complicated arguments. Swift reckoning means complete and effortless divine accounting, not haste that overlooks evidence or justice. His reckoning is both effortless and perfectly complete.

phrases.translation: So if they argue with you ˹O Prophet˺, say, “I have submitted myself to Allah, and so have my followers.”
phrases.explanation: When others dispute with him, the Prophet answers by affirming complete submission to Allah in heart, speech, and action. His followers share that commitment. This response identifies the central issue as devoted obedience to God rather than victory in a sectarian argument. The community’s unity rests upon this shared surrender.

phrases.translation: And ask those who were given the Scripture and the illiterate ˹people˺, “Have you submitted yourselves ˹to Allah˺?”
phrases.explanation: The invitation extends both to people given scripture and to those without a revealed book. No group is excluded from the call to submit to Allah alone. Religious learning or its absence does not remove the need for sincere monotheistic devotion. The same fundamental call addresses every audience.

phrases.translation: If they submit, they will be ˹rightly˺ guided.
phrases.explanation: Those who submit find the path of true guidance. Guidance here is tied to accepting Allah’s oneness and directing worship sincerely to Him. The verse presents submission not as humiliation before people but as the right relationship with the Lord. Such guidance joins belief with willing obedience.

phrases.translation: But if they turn away, then your duty is only to deliver ˹the message˺.
phrases.explanation: If the invited people turn away, the Prophet’s responsibility remains faithful delivery of the message. He is not required to force acceptance or manufacture belief. This limit protects the integrity of the call while leaving each audience responsible for its response. The duty is fulfilled through clear and honest communication.

phrases.translation: And Allah is All-Seeing of ˹His˺ servants
phrases.explanation: Allah sees which servants accept the message and which reject it. His complete observation removes any need for the Prophet to control hidden intentions. Faithful conveyance and human response are both known to God, who judges them with perfect knowledge. Nothing in their response escapes His sight.

phrases.translation: Indeed, those who deny Allah’s signs, kill the prophets unjustly, and kill people who stand up for justice
phrases.explanation: The verse joins denial of Allah’s signs with the killing of prophets and of people who call for justice. These offences reveal violent resistance to divine guidance and to anyone defending what is right. The historical accusation is grave and specific, not a label for ordinary disagreement or for an entire community today.

phrases.translation: —give them good news of a painful punishment
phrases.explanation: The language of good news is an ironic warning, because what awaits these offenders is painful punishment. They are told plainly what their conduct leads to rather than being allowed to imagine lasting impunity. Divine justice includes accountability for violence against God’s messengers and advocates of righteousness.

phrases.translation: They are the ones whose deeds are wasted in this world and the Hereafter.
phrases.explanation: The works of such persistent rejecters bring them no lasting good. In this world, their hidden wrongdoing is exposed and their record becomes one of disgrace rather than honour. In the Hereafter, deeds rooted in denial and injustice do not earn reward. What appeared productive is shown to be empty.

phrases.translation: And they will have no helpers
phrases.explanation: No supporter can rescue them from Allah when He judges their crimes. Human allies may offer protection in worldly conflicts, but they have no power to reverse divine judgment. The absence of helpers completes the picture of works wasted and false security removed. Their isolation on that Day is complete.

phrases.translation: Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scriptures?
phrases.explanation: The question draws attention to people who possessed a share of revealed knowledge. Having access to scripture created responsibility, not automatic righteousness. Their example shows that familiarity with a sacred text means little when its teachings are accepted only while they agree with personal interests.

phrases.translation: Yet when they are invited to the Book of Allah to settle their disputes, some of them turn away heedlessly
phrases.explanation: When invited to let Allah’s Book settle a dispute, some turned away in aversion. Several historical disputes are possible, so the passage should not be reduced to one certain incident. Its clear point is the wrongdoing of rejecting revealed judgment when it contradicts a preferred position.

phrases.translation: This is because they say, “The Fire will not touch us except for a few days.”
phrases.explanation: Their claim that the Fire would touch them for only a few days gave them false confidence to resist divine judgment. This assurance rested on inherited fabrications rather than an authentic divine promise. Treating punishment as brief and guaranteed to end made continued disobedience appear safe.

phrases.translation: They have been deceived in their faith by their wishful lying
phrases.explanation: Wishful inventions deceived them within their religion because they repeated comforting claims as though Allah had revealed them. Desire replaced evidence. The warning applies wherever people manufacture assurances about salvation to avoid repentance, instead of allowing revealed truth to correct their hopes. Such self-deception can become deeply habitual.

phrases.translation: But how ˹horrible˺ will it be when We gather them together on the Day about which there is no doubt
phrases.explanation: The question imagines the dreadful condition of those who turned away when Allah gathers everyone on a Day whose arrival is certain. Present excuses will not prevent that assembly. The warning shifts attention from winning a temporary dispute to standing before God with one’s actual record.

phrases.translation: —when every soul will be paid in full for what it has done, and none will be wronged
phrases.explanation: Every soul will receive the full recompense of what it has done, with no injustice. Nobody will be denied a deserved good deed or punished for another person’s wrong. This perfect equity answers false assurances and assures believers that Allah’s gathering is governed by exact justice.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “O Allah! Lord over all authorities!
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is taught to address Allah as the true Lord of all sovereignty. Every form of authority exists within His dominion rather than as an independent power. Beginning with this title places political rise and fall under God’s rule and teaches believers to approach Him with humility.

phrases.translation: You give authority to whoever You please and remove it from who You please;
phrases.explanation: Allah grants authority to whomever He wills and removes it from whomever He wills. Human rulers therefore possess no permanent or self-created dominion. This truth challenges pride in power and despair under weakness, since every period of rule remains subject to divine permission and wisdom.

phrases.translation: You honour whoever You please and disgrace who You please
phrases.explanation: Honour and disgrace are also under Allah’s control, including the changes associated with gaining or losing authority. People should not measure His approval by status alone. The prayer directs attention to the One who changes circumstances rather than treating powerful people as the ultimate source of worth.

phrases.translation: —all good is in Your Hands.
phrases.explanation: All good is within Allah’s power and gift. His giving does not depend on the permission of another sovereign, and His generosity is not constrained by human institutions. This confession encourages believers to seek good from Him while recognizing that His wisdom determines its forms and timing.

phrases.translation: Surely You ˹alone˺ are Most Capable of everything
phrases.explanation: Nothing lies outside Allah’s ability, whether changing rulers, honouring the lowly, or bringing about what people cannot imagine. The statement grounds the whole prayer in complete divine power. It does not make human choices irrelevant, but denies that any creature can limit what God is able to do.

phrases.translation: You cause the night to pass into the day and the day into the night.
phrases.explanation: Allah makes night enter day and day enter night, changing their lengths and bringing each after the other. This ordered alternation displays the same sovereignty praised in the previous verse. What people experience as a regular cycle remains an ongoing act of divine government. No ruler controls this daily transformation.

phrases.translation: You bring forth the living from the dead and the dead from the living.
phrases.explanation: Allah brings living beings from what is lifeless and brings forth what dies from the living. Created life and reproduction are among the implications of this divine power. In every case, the contrast points to His unique power over life, death, and transformations that no creature can independently command.

phrases.translation: And You provide for whoever You will without limit.”
phrases.explanation: Allah provides for whomever He wills without measure or fear of exhaustion. His treasuries are not reduced by generosity. This assurance teaches dependence upon Him rather than upon changing authorities, while leaving people responsible to receive provision gratefully and use it in obedience. His gifts remain under His wise decree.

phrases.translation: Believers should not take disbelievers as guardians instead of the believers
phrases.explanation: Believers are forbidden to make persistent opponents of faith their protecting allies in place of the believing community. The concern is loyalty that turns against one’s faith and fellow believers, not ordinary kindness, justice, or peaceful dealings. Religious commitment must not be surrendered for protection or advantage.

phrases.translation: —and whoever does so will have nothing to hope for from Allah
phrases.explanation: Whoever enters such disloyal guardianship separates himself from the protection and fellowship hoped for from Allah. The warning is severe because it concerns allegiance, not a minor social preference. A believer cannot expect to oppose the community of faith while remaining entitled to the privileges of loyal membership.

phrases.translation: —unless it is a precaution against their tyranny.
phrases.explanation: An exception exists for genuine precaution against threatened harm. The allowance addresses real fear and vulnerability rather than offering blanket permission for deception or betrayal. Its limits should be judged honestly, without using a distant possibility of danger to justify disloyalty in ordinary circumstances. Necessity must not be exaggerated for convenience.

phrases.translation: And Allah warns you about Himself.
phrases.explanation: Allah warns believers about Himself so that they avoid disobedience and alliances hostile to His guidance. The warning calls for self-examination before hidden loyalty becomes action. Fear of God here means taking His judgment seriously, not living in panic or suspicion of everyone outside the community.

phrases.translation: And to Allah is the final return
phrases.explanation: Everyone will finally return to Allah for reckoning. That return makes the choice of protectors morally significant beyond immediate safety. No alliance can accompany a person as an independent defence on that Day. The verse therefore ends by placing every relationship under divine judgment. Every hidden allegiance will then be uncovered.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Whether you conceal what is in your hearts or reveal it, it is known to Allah.
phrases.explanation: Allah knows what hearts conceal just as fully as what speech and action reveal. In context, this includes hidden loyalty contrary to the preceding command. Secrecy cannot protect an intention from God. The verse calls for inward sincerity rather than outward obedience masking an opposite attachment.

phrases.translation: For He knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth.
phrases.explanation: Divine knowledge covers everything in the heavens and earth, not only the private thoughts of those addressed. This universal scope leaves no hidden corner beyond His awareness. It also confirms that He knows every circumstance surrounding human choices, so His judgment is fully informed. His knowledge is never partial or uninformed.

phrases.translation: And Allah is Most Capable of everything.”
phrases.explanation: Allah has power over everything He knows, including the ability to reward, punish, and change circumstances. Knowledge and ability belong together here. Hidden actions are neither unseen nor beyond His reach, which makes sincere repentance wiser than relying on concealment. Therefore no secret places a person outside divine accountability.

phrases.translation: ˹Watch for˺ the Day when every soul will be presented with whatever good it has done.
phrases.explanation: On the Day of Judgment, every soul will find its good deeds present before it. Nothing righteous is lost or forgotten. The image of deeds brought forward makes accountability concrete and offers reassurance to those who acted sincerely even when their goodness received no public recognition.

phrases.translation: And it will wish that its misdeeds were far off.
phrases.explanation: A person will wish to be far separated from past misdeeds when their consequences become undeniable. Regret on that Day cannot rewrite the record. The warning encourages repentance and repair now, while distance from sin is still possible through changed conduct and divine mercy. Their former choices will then stand plainly before them.

phrases.translation: And Allah warns you about Himself.
phrases.explanation: Allah’s warning about Himself tells people to avoid meeting Him in anger over unrepented disobedience. It is an act of guidance that exposes consequences before they occur. Taking the warning seriously means examining actions rather than presuming upon status or verbal profession. Such warning offers people an opportunity to change.

phrases.translation: And Allah is Ever Gracious to ˹His˺ servants
phrases.explanation: Allah is gracious and merciful to His servants, and the warning itself is part of that compassion. He tells them what harms them and calls them back before judgment. Justice and kindness meet here, since divine mercy includes both forgiveness and clear instruction that protects people from ruin.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “If you ˹sincerely˺ love Allah, then follow me;
phrases.explanation: A claim to love Allah is tested through willingness to follow His Messenger. In this passage, verbal devotion is not accepted as a substitute for faithful response. Following Muhammad means receiving what he brought from Allah and allowing that guidance to shape worship and conduct.

phrases.translation: Allah will love you and forgive your sins.
phrases.explanation: Allah promises His love and forgiveness to those whose faith becomes sincere discipleship. This is an invitation rather than a demand for perfection. People come with sins and shortcomings, yet following divine guidance opens the way to pardon and a restored relationship with their Lord.

phrases.translation: For Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.”
phrases.explanation: Allah’s forgiveness and mercy make the promise accessible to repentant believers. He does not merely expose the gap between professed love and actual obedience. He also offers pardon when people turn toward Him. The names encourage hope while preserving the need for sincere change. Divine generosity answers those who sincerely turn back.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Obey Allah and His Messenger.”
phrases.explanation: The command joins obedience to Allah with obedience to the Messenger He sent. The Prophet’s instruction is followed because he conveys divine guidance, not because he independently claims divine status. This order protects both monotheism and faithful adherence to revelation. Obedience therefore joins inward faith with practical response.

phrases.translation: If they still turn away, then truly Allah does not like the disbelievers
phrases.explanation: Turning away after the truth has been recognized is an act of disbelief, and Allah does not love such rejection. The warning concerns deliberate refusal of His guidance, not people who are still seeking understanding. It makes the audience responsible for its response to the Messenger.

phrases.translation: Indeed, Allah chose Adam, Noah, the family of Abraham, and the family of ’Imrân
phrases.explanation: Allah selected Adam and Noah, together with the households of Abraham and Imran, for a special place in His guidance. Their distinction is tied to true religion and complete submission to Allah. Their honour therefore comes from divine choice and faithfulness rather than ordinary social rank. Their stories form part of one history of guidance.

phrases.translation: above all people ˹of their time˺
phrases.explanation: Their distinction is above the people of their respective times, not an excuse for descendants to claim automatic superiority. Election carries responsibility to uphold Allah’s way. The verse introduces a family history in which sincere worship matters more than genealogy alone. Honour before Allah is not merely a family possession.

phrases.translation: They are descendants of one another.
phrases.explanation: These chosen households are connected through descent, one branch coming from another. The description prepares for the story of Mary and her family within a broader history of faith. It presents continuity across generations without implying that every descendant inherits righteousness automatically. Their shared lineage frames the narrative that follows.

phrases.translation: And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing
phrases.explanation: Allah hears every word and knows every intention, including the dedication and prayers about to be mentioned. These attributes fit the transition into a narrative of supplication and surprising gifts. Nothing in the family’s devotion, hope, or private need is outside His awareness. He therefore responds with complete understanding.

phrases.translation: ˹Remember˺ when the wife of ’Imrân said, “My Lord! I dedicate what is in my womb entirely to Your service, so accept it from me.
phrases.explanation: Imran’s wife vows the child in her womb to Allah’s service, setting the child apart from other occupations for worship and care of the sanctuary. She then asks Allah to accept her offering. Her dedication expresses sincere intention while acknowledging that acceptance belongs to God alone.

phrases.translation: You ˹alone˺ are truly the All-Hearing, All-Knowing.”
phrases.explanation: She calls upon Allah as the One who hears her spoken prayer and knows her inward purpose. Her vow is not hidden from Him, and neither is the sincerity behind it. These names make the prayer personal and attentive, grounding hope in God’s complete awareness.

phrases.translation: When she delivered, she said, “My Lord! I have given birth to a girl,”
phrases.explanation: After giving birth, Mary’s mother tells her Lord that the child is a girl. She had apparently expected a son for the particular service she imagined. Her words are honest about the unexpected outcome while continuing the prayer rather than withdrawing her dedication. She remains engaged in faithful conversation with God.

phrases.translation: —and Allah fully knew what she had delivered
phrases.explanation: Allah already knew exactly what she had delivered. This reminder prevents readers from treating the child’s sex as a mistake or a reduction of her worth. Divine knowledge and acceptance govern the story, not the mother’s limited expectation about how her vow would be fulfilled.

phrases.translation: —“and the male is not like the female.
phrases.explanation: The mother recognizes that the female child is not the male she had envisioned for sanctuary service. The statement concerns the different circumstance before her, not a verdict that women are spiritually inferior. Mary’s subsequent acceptance shows that God can honour her beyond human expectation.

phrases.translation: I have named her Mary, and I seek Your protection for her and her offspring from Satan, the accursed.”
phrases.explanation: She names her daughter Mary and asks Allah to protect her and her descendants from Satan. The vow of service becomes a request for spiritual guardianship. Her concern reaches beyond formal dedication to the child’s life, future, and vulnerability to evil. The mother entrusts their spiritual welfare to Allah.

phrases.translation: So her Lord accepted her graciously and blessed her with a pleasant upbringing
phrases.explanation: Allah accepts Mary with gracious approval and grants her a beautiful upbringing. The answer to her mother’s dedication exceeds the expectations surrounding her birth. Growth here includes being nurtured under divine care, showing that sincere offerings can be accepted in ways people had not planned.

phrases.translation: —entrusting her to the care of Zachariah.
phrases.explanation: Zachariah is entrusted with Mary’s care, giving her protection and responsible guardianship within the sanctuary. Divine acceptance does not leave her without human support. Allah provides for her through both a faithful caretaker and the unusual provision that the narrative goes on to describe. Her upbringing therefore joins devotion with loving protection.

phrases.translation: Whenever Zachariah visited her in the sanctuary, he found her supplied with provisions. He exclaimed, “O Mary! Where did this come from?”
phrases.explanation: Whenever Zachariah visits, he finds provisions with Mary and asks where they came from. His question shows that this supply was not ordinary assistance he had arranged. The provision included fruits outside their usual season, making the scene a sign of Allah’s generous care. Zachariah recognizes something beyond ordinary routine.

phrases.translation: She replied, “It is from Allah.
phrases.explanation: Mary answers that the provision is from Allah. She directs attention away from herself and toward the true Giver. Her response displays faith and understanding, recognizing that what reaches her without an ordinary human cause still has a source in divine generosity. Her brief answer expresses confident and grateful faith.

phrases.translation: Surely Allah provides for whoever He wills without limit.”
phrases.explanation: Allah provides for whomever He wills without being limited by normal expectations or fear of exhaustion. Mary’s answer becomes a general confession of divine abundance. It also prepares Zachariah to hope that God can answer his own apparently impossible longing for a child. This truth soon strengthens Zachariah’s own prayer.

phrases.translation: Then and there Zachariah prayed to his Lord, saying, “My Lord! Grant me—by your grace—righteous offspring.
phrases.explanation: Seeing Mary’s extraordinary provision prompts Zachariah to pray immediately for righteous offspring from Allah. He asks despite his age and his wife’s barrenness because the scene has shown him that customary limits do not confine God. His request seeks a blessed child, not merely descendants.

phrases.translation: You are certainly the Hearer of ˹all˺ prayers.”
phrases.explanation: Zachariah affirms that Allah hears and answers supplication. This confession expresses trust before the answer has appeared. Prayer is therefore not an attempt to inform an unaware God, but an act of hope directed toward One who already knows the need and is able to respond.

phrases.translation: So the angels called out to him while he stood praying in the sanctuary,
phrases.explanation: The angels address Zachariah while he is standing in prayer within the sanctuary. The timing connects the good news with a moment of worship and humble request. His devotion does not earn God’s gift as a transaction, but it forms the setting in which the promise is announced.

phrases.translation: “Allah gives you good news of ˹the birth of˺ John who will confirm the Word of Allah
phrases.explanation: Allah announces John and describes him as confirming the Word from Him, which is understood here as referring to Jesus. John’s mission will affirm God’s truth rather than compete with another prophet. The promise therefore places his coming within a united divine purpose. His role supports the same divine message.

phrases.translation: and will be a great leader, chaste, and a prophet among the righteous.”
phrases.explanation: John will be noble in knowledge and worship, chaste in his conduct, and a prophet among the righteous. These qualities describe the character of the promised son before his birth. The gift is not only a child, but a servant distinguished by devotion and moral discipline.

phrases.translation: Zachariah exclaimed, “My Lord! How can I have a son when I am very old and my wife is barren?”
phrases.explanation: Zachariah asks how he can have a son when old age and his wife’s barrenness make it ordinarily impossible. His question expresses amazement at the promise rather than settled rejection. He measures the news by familiar human limits, preparing for an answer about God’s greater power.

phrases.translation: He replied, “So will it be.
phrases.explanation: The answer assures him that matters will occur as Allah has determined. Divine creation is not restricted by the circumstances that make the birth seem impossible to him. The One who created Zachariah and his wife can grant them a child through means beyond expectation.

phrases.translation: Allah does what He wills.”
phrases.explanation: Allah accomplishes whatever He wills, and no created limitation can defeat His purpose. This principle applies to the promised birth without making every human wish a guaranteed miracle. Zachariah receives a specific divine promise, and the verse explains why that promise is completely reliable. His will is never constrained by human expectation.

phrases.translation: Zachariah said, “My Lord! Grant me a sign.”
phrases.explanation: Zachariah asks for a mark that will confirm the astonishing announcement and settle his heart. The request shows how extraordinary the promise seemed to him. Allah answers with a sign connected to Zachariah himself, making the confirmation personal, visible, and impossible to dismiss as an ordinary occurrence.

phrases.translation: He said, “Your sign is that you will not ˹be able to˺ speak to people for three days except through gestures.
phrases.explanation: For three days, Zachariah will be unable to address people except through gestures. This restriction serves as the promised mark rather than an ordinary loss of speech through illness. His silence gives the good news a concrete confirmation while allowing necessary communication in another form.

phrases.translation: Remember your Lord often and glorify ˹Him˺ morning and evening.”
phrases.explanation: The inability to converse does not prevent remembrance and glorification of Allah. Zachariah is instructed to increase devotion morning and evening, turning the period of silence toward worship. Ordinary conversation pauses, but his relationship with God continues through frequent praise and attentive remembrance. Silence becomes an opportunity for concentrated devotion.

phrases.translation: And ˹remember˺ when the angels said, “O Mary! Surely Allah has selected you, purified you,
phrases.explanation: The angels announce that Allah has selected and purified Mary through His grace. Her distinction comes from divine choice and the devotion He has nurtured in her. The announcement prepares her for a remarkable responsibility without suggesting that she possesses independent divinity. Her story therefore remains one of grateful servanthood.

phrases.translation: and chosen you over all women of the world
phrases.explanation: Mary is chosen above the women of her world for the unique honour entrusted to her. Such selection is Allah’s gift, not a rank she grants herself. The verse calls readers to respect her devotion and special role while keeping worship directed to Allah alone.

phrases.translation: O Mary! Be devout to your Lord
phrases.explanation: Mary is commanded to devote her obedience sincerely to her Lord. Her election is therefore joined with responsibility, not passive privilege. The special announcement she receives calls for deeper worship and faithfulness. Devotion remains directed toward Allah rather than toward Mary or any other created person.

phrases.translation: prostrate yourself ˹in prayer˺ and bow along with those who bow down.”
phrases.explanation: Prostration and bowing express humility and submission before Allah. Mary is told to join those who worship in this way, placing her within a community of devotion. Outward prayer embodies the inward obedience just commanded, uniting reverent posture with sincere service to God. Such worship expresses her continuing dedication.

phrases.translation: This is news of the unseen that We reveal to you ˹O Prophet˺.
phrases.explanation: The accounts of Mary, her family, Zachariah, and John are revealed to Muhammad as news of realities he did not witness. Their source is divine knowledge rather than his personal memory or research. This statement directly attributes the historical report to revelation. Revelation thus supplies knowledge beyond human observation.

phrases.translation: You were not with them when they cast lots to decide who would be Mary’s guardian,
phrases.explanation: Muhammad was not present when those responsible for Mary cast lots to determine her guardian. He therefore could not have learned the detail by standing among them. The reminder reinforces that the account reaches him from Allah, who knows both past events and what was hidden from others.

phrases.translation: nor were you there when they argued ˹about it˺
phrases.explanation: He was likewise absent when they disputed over who should care for Mary. The repetition strengthens the evidence that his knowledge is revealed. Details about their rivalry are not presented as eyewitness recollection, but as part of the unseen history Allah chooses to make known.

phrases.translation: ˹Remember˺ when the angels proclaimed, “O Mary! Allah gives you good news of a Word from Him, his name will be the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary;
phrases.explanation: Mary receives news of a son called a Word from Allah, the Messiah Jesus, son of Mary. The title points to his creation through God’s command and does not erase his human birth from Mary. Naming both his titles and his mother identifies him clearly within the narrative.

phrases.translation: honoured in this world and the Hereafter, and he will be one of those nearest ˹to Allah˺
phrases.explanation: Jesus is honoured in this world and the Hereafter and counted among those brought near to Allah. His rank is a gift from God, expressed through prophecy, miracles, and righteous service. Nearness to Allah does not make him Allah, but marks exceptional honour among His servants.

phrases.translation: And he will speak to people in ˹his˺ infancy and adulthood
phrases.explanation: Jesus will speak during infancy and again in mature adulthood. His speech in the cradle is an extraordinary sign, while his later speech belongs to his mission among people. Both stages fall under Allah’s announcement, demonstrating that God can enable speech whenever He wills. His whole life bears witness to divine purpose.

phrases.translation: and will be one of the righteous.”
phrases.explanation: Jesus is also declared to be among the righteous. His miracles and honour therefore accompany moral and spiritual integrity rather than mere spectacle. The description defines his life through faithful service to Allah and prepares readers to understand his works as signs of a righteous messenger.

phrases.translation: Mary wondered, “My Lord! How can I have a child when no man has ever touched me?”
phrases.explanation: Mary asks how she can bear a child when no man has touched her. Her question seeks to understand the manner of an event beyond ordinary experience. It is an honest response to astonishing news, not an accusation or a denial of Allah’s ability. The answer will honor both her innocence and God’s power.

phrases.translation: An angel replied, “So will it be.
phrases.explanation: The angel answers that the matter will unfold as Allah has announced. This assurance moves the discussion from ordinary means to divine creation. Mary is not told to solve the apparent impossibility herself. She is asked to trust the word of the Lord who addresses her.

phrases.translation: Allah creates what He wills.
phrases.explanation: Allah creates whatever He wills, with or without the means people normally expect. He can grant a child without a father just as He can withhold one where ordinary means exist. Creative power belongs to Him, not to the circumstances through which He chooses to act.

phrases.translation: When He decrees a matter, He simply tells it, ‘Be!’ And it is
phrases.explanation: When Allah decrees something, His command brings it into being. The expression Be conveys effortless creative authority rather than a process that created things can resist. Jesus’ conception therefore becomes a sign of divine power while remaining a real event in Mary’s human life. Nothing can frustrate that sovereign creative decision.

phrases.translation: And Allah will teach him writing and wisdom
phrases.explanation: Allah will teach Jesus writing and wisdom. His knowledge is therefore received from God as part of his preparation for prophethood. Wisdom enables him to understand and apply guidance rightly. The verse attributes his learning to divine teaching rather than presenting him as an independent source of knowledge.

phrases.translation: the Torah and the Gospel
phrases.explanation: Jesus will also be taught the Torah and the Gospel. These scriptures connect his mission with earlier revelation and the particular guidance entrusted to him. His teaching confirms God’s continuing purpose rather than establishing an independent religion centred upon his own divinity. He receives and conveys what Allah entrusts to him.

phrases.translation: and ˹make him˺ a messenger to the Children of Israel ˹to proclaim,˺ ‘I have come to you with a sign from your Lord:
phrases.explanation: Jesus is sent as a messenger to the Children of Israel, declaring that his signs come from their Lord. His mission and authority are derived from Allah. He does not call people toward himself as God, but presents evidence that he truthfully conveys God’s message.

phrases.translation: I will make for you a bird from clay, breathe into it, and it will become a ˹real˺ bird
phrases.explanation: Jesus forms a bird from clay and breathes into it, and it becomes a living bird. This extraordinary act demonstrates creative power beyond normal human ability. The repeated qualification that it occurs by Allah’s Will is essential, making the event a divine sign performed through His messenger.

phrases.translation: —by Allah’s Will. I will heal the blind and the leper and raise the dead to life
phrases.explanation: Healing the blind and lepers and raising the dead likewise occur by Allah’s permission. Jesus’ role does not make him independently divine. God brings about these wonders through him, confirming his truthfulness while showing mercy to people who could not rescue themselves from those conditions.

phrases.translation: —by Allah’s Will. And I will prophesize what you eat and store in your houses.
phrases.explanation: Jesus also reports what people eat and store privately in their homes, by Allah’s Will. This knowledge of hidden ordinary matters supports his claim to revelation. This prophetic evidence is entirely different from astrology or guesswork, since its truth and source rest with Allah. The sign reaches even their private domestic lives.

phrases.translation: Surely in this is a sign for you if you ˹truly˺ believe
phrases.explanation: These signs call people to recognize that Jesus speaks truthfully as God’s messenger. Their purpose is faith and reflection, not entertainment or amazement alone. A believing response accepts the evidence, affirms Allah’s oneness, and follows the guidance the signs were sent to confirm. Miracles therefore serve the moral purpose of guidance.

phrases.translation: And I will confirm the Torah revealed before me and legalize some of what had been forbidden to you.
phrases.explanation: Jesus confirms the Torah that came before him and makes lawful some things previously forbidden to his audience. His mission maintains continuity with earlier revelation while introducing the permissions Allah authorizes through him. Any change in legal detail remains subject to God’s command, not personal preference.

phrases.translation: I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, so be mindful of Allah and obey me
phrases.explanation: Because Jesus comes with a sign from their Lord, the people are told to be mindful of Allah and obey him. Obedience to the messenger is an expression of obedience to God who sent him. It involves accepting his teaching and fulfilling the covenant of faithful worship.

phrases.translation: Surely Allah is my Lord and your Lord.
phrases.explanation: Jesus identifies Allah as his own Lord and the Lord of his listeners. This places him within created servanthood rather than above it. He and his audience share the same obligation toward the one true God. The statement directly rules out worshipping Jesus as an independent divine partner.

phrases.translation: So worship Him ˹alone˺.
phrases.explanation: Because Allah alone is Lord, worship must be directed to Him alone. Jesus calls people to the same exclusive devotion taught by God’s messengers. His own miracles and honour do not change that command. They serve to confirm the message rather than redirect worship toward himself.

phrases.translation: This is the Straight Path.’”
phrases.explanation: Worshipping Allah alone and obeying His messenger constitute the straight path. It is straight because it agrees with the truth about God and leads toward Him without distortion. Jesus presents faithful submission, not later claims about his person, as the way of right guidance. This is the consistent direction of God’s message.

phrases.translation: When Jesus sensed disbelief from his people, he asked, “Who will stand up with me for Allah?”
phrases.explanation: When Jesus recognizes rejection among his people, he asks who will support him in Allah’s cause. The request seeks assistance for the divine mission rather than personal power or revenge. Faithful messengers may need companions who stand publicly with truth when opposition becomes firm. Their answer would reveal genuine commitment.

phrases.translation: The disciples replied, “We will stand up for Allah.
phrases.explanation: The disciples answer by calling themselves helpers for Allah. They understand their support of Jesus as service to God’s purpose, not loyalty to a personality above divine guidance. Their response joins practical solidarity with the religious aim for which Jesus was sent. They offer themselves for a sacred duty.

phrases.translation: We believe in Allah, so bear witness that we have submitted.”
phrases.explanation: They affirm belief in Allah and ask Jesus to witness that they have submitted. Their faith is expressed through willing obedience to God and support for His messenger. The verse presents them as sincere servants whose allegiance is defined by submission rather than by later sectarian labels.

phrases.translation: ˹They prayed to Allah,˺ “Our Lord! We believe in Your revelations and follow the messenger,
phrases.explanation: The disciples tell Allah that they believe in what He revealed and that they follow His messenger, Jesus. Faith accepts revelation while discipleship turns it into practice. Their prayer joins trust in God’s message with loyalty to the prophet entrusted to deliver it. Their response therefore includes both conviction and allegiance.

phrases.translation: so count us among those who bear witness.”
phrases.explanation: They ask to be recorded among those who bear witness to truth. This means sharing the honour of people who affirm Allah’s oneness, believe His messengers, and follow His commands. They seek a lasting testimony of faith rather than temporary praise from their contemporaries. It is a request for divine recognition.

phrases.translation: And the disbelievers made a plan ˹against Jesus˺, but Allah also planned
phrases.explanation: Opponents plotted against Jesus after rejecting his message, but Allah brought His own wise purpose to fulfilment. Human schemes do not escape divine knowledge or control. The wording describes a counter-plan that frustrates harm, not deceit for an unjust purpose. The following verses explain how that purpose unfolds.

phrases.translation: —and Allah is the best of planners
phrases.explanation: Allah is best in planning because His knowledge, wisdom, and power are complete. He can protect His messenger and defeat hostile designs without being limited by what opponents intend. The statement reassures believers that malicious planning never has the final word over God’s purpose. His plan always achieves its righteous end.

phrases.translation: ˹Remember˺ when Allah said, “O Jesus! I will take you and raise you up to Myself.
phrases.explanation: Allah announces that He will take Jesus and raise him to Himself. The promise comes in response to the plot against him and affirms divine protection and exaltation. This is understood as Jesus being taken from the earth and raised to Allah, with his life and fate remaining under Allah’s power.

phrases.translation: I will deliver you from those who disbelieve, and elevate your followers above the disbelievers until the Day of Judgment.
phrases.explanation: Allah also promises to cleanse Jesus’ followers from the influence of rejecters and grant them ascendancy over those who deny him until the Day of Judgment. Their distinction rests on following his true message. The promise does not eliminate continuing disagreement, which still awaits final judgment.

phrases.translation: Then to Me you will ˹all˺ return, and I will settle all your disputes
phrases.explanation: Everyone will return to Allah, who will judge the disputes surrounding Jesus with complete truth. Human groups do not have the final authority to settle his status by argument or force. The resurrection will expose error and establish the correct judgment about every contested claim.

phrases.translation: As for those who disbelieve,
phrases.explanation: Those who reject the truth brought by Jesus and oppose his message face the consequence of their own denial. The warning addresses persistent unbelief and false claims, not sincere questions about difficult matters. It sets out the outcome before the contrasting promise to faithful servants.

phrases.translation: I will subject them to a severe punishment in this life and the Hereafter,
phrases.explanation: Their punishment is severe in both this life and the Hereafter. The verse treats accountability as extending beyond visible worldly consequences. Present disgrace or hardship is not the whole story, and no prosperous appearance cancels the final judgment that awaits unrepented rejection. The warning therefore concerns both present and final recompense.

phrases.translation: and they will have no helpers
phrases.explanation: No helper can defend persistent rejecters against Allah’s judgment or remove their punishment. Allies and advocates may influence worldly affairs, but they cannot overrule God. This declaration strips away false hopes of rescue and completes the warning with absolute divine authority. Their ultimate isolation cannot be reversed by human power.

phrases.translation: And as for those who believe and do good, they will be rewarded in full.
phrases.explanation: Those who believe in Allah’s messenger and perform righteous deeds receive their reward in full. Nothing sincere and obedient is reduced or forgotten. Faith and action belong together, since accepting the message involves living by the duties and guidance it brings. Their recompense reflects divine generosity and exact justice.

phrases.translation: And Allah does not like the wrongdoers.”
phrases.explanation: Allah does not love wrongdoing, including denying people their rights or putting things outside their proper place. He will not treat faithful doers of good as though they were persistent wrongdoers. This statement assures readers that divine recompense is just and properly distinguishes conduct. His judgment therefore upholds every valid right.

phrases.translation: We recite ˹all˺ this to you ˹O Prophet˺ as one of the signs
phrases.explanation: Allah recites these reports to Muhammad as signs containing evidence and lessons. The accounts of Jesus, Mary, their families, and their opponents address disputed claims through revealed history. They guide sincere listeners and serve as proof against arguments that contradict the truth. They also affirm the Prophet’s revealed knowledge.

phrases.translation: and ˹as˺ a wise reminder
phrases.explanation: The reports also belong to the wise Reminder, the Qur’an. Their wisdom distinguishes truth from falsehood and directs readers toward right understanding. Recitation therefore has a purpose beyond preserving stories. It calls people to remember God’s guidance and respond with discernment. Its instruction remains relevant beyond the original dispute.

phrases.translation: Indeed, the example of Jesus in the sight of Allah is like that of Adam.
phrases.explanation: Jesus’ case before Allah resembles Adam’s because extraordinary parentage does not imply divinity. Adam was created without a father or mother, while Jesus was created without a father. If divine power accounts for Adam’s existence, the birth of Jesus provides no reason to call him God.

phrases.translation: He created him from dust, then said to him, “Be!” And he was
phrases.explanation: Allah created Adam from dust and brought him into being through His command. This comparison grounds the argument in effortless divine creation. The same God who made Adam could create Jesus from Mary without a male parent, while both remained created servants. Creative command, not parentage, is the decisive point.

phrases.translation: This is the truth from your Lord
phrases.explanation: The account just revealed about Jesus is the truth from Muhammad’s Lord. Its authority comes from divine revelation rather than sectarian argument or human speculation. This declaration settles the source of the report and asks readers to receive it as reliable guidance. The verse therefore calls for confident acceptance.

phrases.translation: so do not be one of those who doubt
phrases.explanation: The Prophet and his audience are told not to join those who doubt this revealed truth. Doubt here means hesitating before what Allah has clearly established, not asking sincere questions to understand it. Confidence is appropriate because the statement rests on God’s knowledge. Revelation gives a firmer basis than conjecture.

phrases.translation: Now, whoever disputes with you ˹O Prophet˺ concerning Jesus after full knowledge has come to you, say, “Come!
phrases.explanation: After revealed knowledge about Jesus has reached the Prophet, continued disputation produces a solemn challenge. The invitation follows clarification rather than replacing it. It addresses determined rejection of the truth just presented, showing how seriously the dispute concerns God and His messenger. The matter has moved beyond unsupported assertion.

phrases.translation: Let us gather our children and your children, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves
phrases.explanation: Both sides are asked to bring their children, women, and themselves. Gathering families makes the occasion weighty and public, with each party standing fully behind its claim. The verse describes a particular prophetic confrontation, not a casual practice for ordinary arguments between individuals. Nobody could treat the appeal lightly.

phrases.translation: —then let us sincerely invoke Allah’s curse upon the liars.”
phrases.explanation: The parties would then pray earnestly for Allah’s curse to fall upon whoever was lying. Judgment is left to God rather than decided through insults or violence. This extreme appeal underscores the duty to speak truthfully about Allah and not persist in fabricated claims. The passage therefore warns against deliberate falsehood.

phrases.translation: Certainly, this is the true narrative, and there is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Allah.
phrases.explanation: The narrative about Jesus is declared true, including his identity as Allah’s servant and messenger. Its central theological conclusion is that no created being shares Allah’s right to worship. The historical account and the confession of monotheism therefore support one another. Nothing else shares His divine authority.

phrases.translation: And indeed, Allah ˹alone˺ is the Almighty, All-Wise
phrases.explanation: Allah is Almighty and All-Wise, with complete power and perfect judgment. These attributes assure readers that the true narrative rests with the sovereign Lord who knows every claim. His wisdom governs revelation, and His might ensures that falsehood cannot overturn His purpose. Truth stands secure under His rule.

phrases.translation: If they turn away
phrases.explanation: If the disputants turn away after the evidence and solemn invitation, their refusal is itself a responsible choice. The verse does not instruct believers to chase them with endless contention. It places the outcome before Allah after the message has been made clear. Responsibility remains with those who reject.

phrases.translation: then surely Allah has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of the corruptors
phrases.explanation: Allah knows those who spread corruption through disobedience and false claims about Him. He records their conduct and will requite it justly. His knowledge covers both open argument and hidden motive, so turning away does not remove anyone from accountability. No corrupt motive escapes His record.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “O People of the Book! Let us come to common terms: that we will worship none but Allah,
phrases.explanation: The People of the Book are invited to a just common principle: worship none but Allah. The appeal begins with a truth that divine messengers share rather than with partisan labels. It seeks agreement around exclusive devotion to the one God. This principle offers a sincere basis for dialogue.

phrases.translation: associate none with Him, nor take one another as lords instead of Allah.”
phrases.explanation: Common worship also requires rejecting every partner with Allah and refusing to treat other human beings as lords independent of Him. Religious leaders cannot authorize disobedience to God or claim divine rights. Obedience to people must always remain under Allah’s authority. No messenger ever possessed that independent lordship.

phrases.translation: But if they turn away, then say, “Bear witness that we have submitted ˹to Allah alone˺.”
phrases.explanation: If they decline this common confession, the believers are to state clearly that they have submitted to Allah. The response establishes their position without pretending agreement exists. Their identity rests on submission to God rather than on winning the other party’s approval. The believers remain faithful to their confession.

phrases.translation: O People of the Book! Why do you argue about Abraham, while the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until long after him?
phrases.explanation: Disputing over Abraham’s religious identity ignores chronology, since the Torah and Gospel were revealed long after him. The later scriptures cannot make him a member of communities organized around them before they existed. The question exposes a claim driven by affiliation rather than historical understanding.

phrases.translation: Do you not understand
phrases.explanation: The rebuke asks whether the disputants will use their reason. Evidence about sequence and revelation should lead them to reconsider their claims. The appeal is intellectual as well as spiritual, inviting reflection instead of loyalty to inherited assertions that cannot fit the facts. Reason should correct inherited partisan claims.

phrases.translation: Here you are! You disputed about what you have ˹little˺ knowledge of, but why do you now argue about what you have no knowledge of?
phrases.explanation: The disputants had already argued about matters within their knowledge, yet now they argue about Abraham without evidence. Their confidence exceeds what their scriptures or experience can support. The verse distinguishes responsible interpretation from confident speech about matters one does not actually know. Such argument reveals attachment rather than knowledge.

phrases.translation: Allah knows and you do not know
phrases.explanation: Allah knows Abraham’s reality, while the disputants do not. This contrast makes humility necessary and removes the basis for competing claims. When human knowledge reaches its limit, people should accept correction from divine revelation instead of treating speculation as certainty. His knowledge is complete and theirs is limited.

phrases.translation: Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian;
phrases.explanation: Abraham cannot properly be claimed as a Jew or Christian in the later communal senses disputed here. The statement releases him from rival attempts to possess his legacy. His significance is established by God’s account rather than by the labels of groups that came afterward.

phrases.translation: he submitted in all uprightness and was not a polytheist
phrases.explanation: Abraham was upright, wholly submitted to Allah, and free from polytheism. These qualities define his religion positively. He directed faith and worship toward the one God without partners, providing the pattern by which claims to follow him should be measured. His example centres upon sincere monotheism.

phrases.translation: Indeed, those who have the best claim to Abraham are his followers, this Prophet, and the believers.
